missionPremise: unchanged from CP1: the reaper's start-time fallback attached a finished sibling (czlpc) to the running Hays publish 41bcc81a and terminated it crashed mid-bake; the run's own close then failed on 23505 while publish_runs and the walk say it succeeded. Identity replaces the heuristic.
completionPredicate: unchanged from CP1; evaluated at close.
scopeBasis: unchanged from CP1, with one addition made during the build and named here: the loop's child naming was widened from an unconditional stamp to nameChildRun (a present name is never overwritten; a disagreement between the parent's API-response name and the child's own CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION is recorded as a run_event and fails the county as TX-CONFORMANT-FAILED / EXECUTION_NAME_MISMATCH). Reason: on the gcloud --wait path the child runs and names itself before the loop's stamp lands, and an unconditional stamp would have overwritten the child's own name, which is exactly the two-writers shape this card kills.

selfReviewFindings.finding: reaper.mjs terminate() wrote runs.status a second time after writeTermination had already written status = exit_kind (card A leftover, two writers of one field); surfaced by the three-sibling test expecting exactly one status write
selfReviewFindings.fix: the reaper's own UPDATE removed; writeTermination is the one writer; card A's orphan tests still see the status write

selfReviewFindings.finding: the first loop change stamped the child unconditionally from the API response; on the gcloud --wait path the child has already named itself and the stamp would overwrite it
selfReviewFindings.fix: nameChildRun: never overwrites a present name, confirms agreement (execution_confirmed_by_parent), records a disagreement as run_event execution-name-disagreement and the loop fails that county as TX-CONFORMANT-FAILED / EXECUTION_NAME_MISMATCH; tested at unit level and at loop level
